subject: Curelytics — performance gating plan & GPU concurrency recommendation
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@curelytics.ai>, Maya Torres <maya@curelytics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jul 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — performance gating & next steps

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and proposal for next steps so we stay aligned on the performance requirements you outlined. Short version: we can meet your latency/streaming goals, but need to validate on a dedicated pilot and pick the right GPU/throughput reservation to hit p95 targets cost-effectively.

Key constraints you mentioned
- Target p95 latency: <= 120ms for average request (<=512 tokens output)
- Sustained throughput target: 200 req/s during business-hours bursts
- Concurrency: typical concurrent users ~40–60, peak spikes to ~120 for short windows
- Streaming: incremental token flush is required (sub-200ms partial chunks)
- Payload: median prompt size ~180 tokens; long tails up to ~2k tokens

Our initial recommendation (to validate in pilot)
- Pilot mode: 2-week dedicated pilot using a reserved slab we control; run production-like traffic replays + small A/B of batching configs
- GPU shortlist to evaluate: H100 (best for throughput/streaming with nvlink), A100-80GB (stable baseline), and L40S (cost-effective for heavy quantization)
- Reserved throughput target for pilot: 250 req/s headroom to validate autoscaling + burst handling
- Concurrency plan: reserve capacity to sustain ~120 short spikes with admission control + overflow routing to hosted fallback model

Data and artifacts we need from your side
1) Sample payloads/logs (we'll use these to build the workload replay) — ideally 24–72h of representative traffic (anonymized).
2) Priority prompt set / canary evals to validate output quality after quantization.
3) Any regulatory constraints re: on-prem or VPC (PII handling, logging policies).

Next steps
- Samir: share the anonymized sample payloads (curelytics-sample-payloads.jsonl) — target: EOD Tue (2028-07-09)
- Ben/Aditya: I'll loop you in to scope perf test harness and pilot acceptance criteria
- I'll prepare a short pilot MOP (attached draft) and a DocuSign pilot agreement link for signatures.

Attachments: curelytics-demo-notes.pdf, pilot-mop-draft.docx

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow if you want to walk through the pilot plan line-by-line.

— Kimberly Park
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
From: Samir Gupta <samir@curelytics.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Torres <maya@curelytics.ai>
Date: Sat, 6 Jul 2028 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — performance gating & next steps

Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary. We're on board with a 2-week dedicated pilot. Quick responses inline below and attaching logs/payloads.

- Payloads/logs: attached curelytics-sample-payloads.jsonl (anonymized). The file contains 48h of traffic, peak window on day 2 (approx 10–11am PT).
- p95 target: 120ms is strict but represents our user-facing SLA — some endpoints (short chat) are more sensitive than others.
- Streaming: we need token-level partial responses for the chat product; typical chunk size is 60–90ms in production.
- Compliance: we are ok with VPC deployment; logs should be stored for 30 days and then deleted.

A couple of asks from our side
1) Can Redwood run the pilot on H100 and A100 and provide a short report with p50/p95/p99 and token throughput for streaming?
2) We may want a conservative pricing cap during pilot — can you confirm an estimate for the 2-week reserved slab?
3) Who will own acceptance criteria? We propose: p95 <= 150ms (pilot acceptance) and p95 <= 120ms for go-live.

Attaching: curelytics-sample-payloads.jsonl

Samir
Head of Platform
Curelytics
samir@curelytics.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@curelytics.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — performance gating & next steps

Thanks Samir — received the payloads. High-level tech notes and proposed acceptance / sizing approach below.

On the GPU choice
- H100: best candidate for streaming + high token throughput due to NVLink + larger L2. Expect strongest p95 headroom for concurrent streaming sessions. Downside: higher effective cost.
- A100-80GB: predictable, excellent for larger context windows (2k tokens). Good stability for batching-heavy workloads.
- L40S: promising when we apply 4-bit or 8-bit quantization — lower cost, but we need to validate quality regressions against your prompt set.

Pilot sizing suggestion (how we run the two-week test)
1) Baseline run on A100-80GB: replay 48h payload, 1.0x speed for full-day baseline. Measure p50/p95/p99, token/sec, KB/sec of KV cache hit rate.
2) Streaming test on H100: focus on the 10–11am peak window, run with streaming enabled and partial chunk thresholds at 60ms/90ms to emulate your UI.
3) Quantized pass on L40S: run the priority prompt set (canary evals) to measure quality delta.

Acceptance criteria (pilot)
- Functional: streaming partial-chunk latency < 200ms and correct ordering of token deltas
- Performance: pilot p95 <= 150ms (as Samir suggested) for standard traffic; p50 < 40ms desirable
- Throughput: platform can sustain 250 req/s for 10-minute sustained windows without queue growth
- Quality: top-10 canary prompts must not regress more than X% BLEU/embedding-similarity threshold (we'll define exact metric with your team)

Operational asks from Redwood side
- We'll need a short service account/key and an S3-like drop for logs (we'll provide instructions).
- We'll propose a reserved slab cost estimate by EOD Mon (2028-07-08). If you need a firm cap during pilot, we can add a spend guard.

Next steps (proposed cadence)
- Samir: confirm payload receipt and permission to run replays (reply all).
- Kimberly: I'll schedule a 30m kickoff with Curelytics ops and our perf team for Tue 10am PT to align on acceptance metrics.
- Aditya/Ben: we'll prepare the test harness and bring initial cost numbers.

— Ben Carter
